summary:
Wales stands under the United Kingdom framework for legal gender recognition, equality law and sex-based segregation in custody. The Senedd's devolved competence runs through health, education and equality delivery, so a visitor's legal status is set nationally while Welsh institutions determine which services and protections are actually available.

Devolved policy does not extend to legal gender recognition, equality legislation or prisons. The marker rules, single-sex space enforcement and custody segregation a visitor encounters in Wales are set by the national framework rather than by Welsh ministers.

The Welsh Government's LGBTQ+ Action Plan for Wales, published in February 2023, states the aim of making Wales the most LGBTQ+ friendly nation in Europe. It commits the devolved administration to pursue a Welsh-specific ban on conversion practices; a Working Group on Banning Conversion Practices was formed in December 2022 and the government published its banning conversion practices document in May 2024.

Transgender healthcare in Wales was historically delivered by referral to clinics in London. The first Welsh gender identity clinic opened in September 2019, ending the default referral of Welsh adults outside Wales.

The Welsh Government's LGBTQ+ Action Plan document for young people, posted in January 2026, forms part of the standing devolved inclusion programme. The programme's update page addresses the For Women Scotland judgment of 19 December 2025.
tangentialFactors:
The LGBTQ+ Action Plan records the UK Government's blocking of the Gender Recognition Reform (Scotland) Bill in January 2023, an adjacent jurisdiction's reform stopped at national level. The episode marks the limit of what a devolved administration can legislate on gender recognition.

Welsh policy ambition and the legal position diverge. The Action Plan's stated goal sits alongside national rules on gender recognition and single-sex spaces that apply in Wales and that the devolved administration cannot alter.
localsOnly:
The LGBTQ+ Action Plan for Wales was announced in the Senedd on 21 June 2022 by Deputy Minister Hannah Blythyn under the 2021 Welsh Labour-Plaid Cymru agreement. It was built on 61 recommendations from the Independent LGBTQ+ Expert Panel of March 2021 and a 12-week public consultation that drew 1,328 responses, and it funds a Grassroots Pride Fund.

Statutory school guidance issued for consultation in May 2025, Rights, Respect, Equality, obliges schools to challenge bullying and harassment on the grounds of sex, gender reassignment and sexual orientation. It requires incidents to be recorded and monitored and provides a route for parents to escalate complaints.

Welsh NHS commissioners stated in March 2024 that they had no plans to develop a children's gender service, and parents of transgender children called for more help.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether a Welsh-specific ban on conversion practices has been enacted, and what it covers, is not established by these sources. The material records the commitment, the working group formed in December 2022 and the government's May 2024 document.

The content of the Welsh Government's response to the For Women Scotland judgment of 19 December 2025 is not sourced here; only the existence of the programme update page is recorded.

No policing, custody, hate-crime prosecution or trans-specific violence data specific to Wales appears in these sources. Those matters fall to the United Kingdom framework.
